Nine new litter bins put in, emptied and maintained: on Jersey Road, Brokesby Road, Bonymaen Road, Cefn Road, Caldicot Road, Mansel Road, Lan Coed and Chirk Gardens.
A no fly-tipping sign put up at Chepstow Place.
A fallen pine tree cleared and three more felled on Buckingham Road.
New street name plates on Talfan Road.

The leisure centre at Cefn Hengoed upgraded as part of the same £7.5m scheme, with a new gym, a refurbished sports hall and community rooms.
Bonymaen Park playground given a new safety surface and new equipment.
Brokesby Road playground upgraded.
A new safety surface and carousel at the Cwm playground.
More than £150,000 invested in the ward's play areas.
New fencing opposite the Brokesby Road playground and high bollards in Bonymaen Park, from our community budget.

Daffodil bulbs planted at sites across the ward every autumn.
A new tree planted on Lan Coed in Winch Wen.
Timber bollards and boulders put in to protect verges and green areas, including 35 bollards on Jersey Road, 15 on Cwm Chapel Road, and at Pen-y-Garn and Colwyn Road.

Donations to Kilvey Writers, Manic Productions and Bonymaen Kids Play Initiative.
Support for FC Bonymaen and Bonymaen Colts FC.
A family engagement centre created at Cefn Hengoed Community School.
New facilities for pupils with additional learning needs at Cwm Glas Primary School.
Pentrechwyth Primary School rewired, with a new fire alarm.
More than £970,000 invested in the ward's schools since 2022.
Surgeries twice a month, both at 7pm: the first Monday at Bonymaen Community Centre and the third Monday at Bonymaen Rugby Club.

pledges.title: Invest in our community

done: Organising and running a monthly Sunday Kids Club at Dunvant Social Centre.
Organising and running a weekly summer breakfast club for families at Dunvant Social Centre.

Secured funding for a new community Pétanque Piste at Dunvant Park, funded a sign explaining the rules for all users, and organised an introductory session and a Bastille Day fun tournament with bread, cheese and French music, working with Friends of Dunvant Park.
Annual supporter of Dunvant Horticultural Society Show, honoured to be asked to present prizes and draw the raffle.

Secretary of Friends of Dunvant Park and very active volunteer, helping to organise and run fun days every summer and autumn, weekly summer Free Play Friday sessions, annual Carols in the Park, monthly volunteer days and other activities.
Helping to fund Killay Community Council and Swansea Bay Street Market's now regular Killay Market in the Precinct to keep pitch costs down for traders. Also helping to produce posters for the event.

Organising and running toy share events at Dunvant Social Centre and Killay Scout and Guides HQ.

Part-funded new interpretation panels along the Old Carriage Drive path to share the history of the area with path users.

Organising and running weekly Warm Hub sessions over the winter at Dunvant Social Centre, bringing the community together for hot drinks, refreshments, stretching and tai chi sessions, and information from local organisations.
Organising Christmas hampers for local residents with Tonia Antoniazzi MP and the Sharing Table, making a donation to help fund them and delivering them over the Christmas period.

Organising and helping to run the Annual Community Christmas Afternoon Tea at Dunvant Social Centre, bringing together local organisations including churches, chapels, WI, Horticultural Society, Dunvant Male Choir and Clyne Valley Community Project to share their activities and encourage new members. Helping Ty Cila to arrange a visit from Father Christmas and Mrs Claus at their Christmas party.
Organising and distributing Christmas supermarket vouchers for families and individuals who may be struggling at this costly time of year.
Patron of the historic Dunvant Male Choir and regular attendee at their concerts.

Committee member and regular volunteer with Nant Cillan Project, which aims to maintain and enhance the area around Dunvant Social Centre, the Scout Hut and Ebeneser Chapel, with the Cillan stream at its centre.
Organised a very successful and well-attended VE Day 80 celebration at Dunvant Social Centre.
Donated funds from my community budget to help Dunvant Social Centre install new flooring.
Helping to run the monthly Community Cinema and Chat at Dunvant Social Centre, giving residents the opportunity to catch up over a cuppa and enjoy a good film on the big screen.
Regular attendee at Killay Community Council meetings and supporter of its community events, including the One Killay multicultural showcase day and St David's Day singing in the Precinct.
Volunteer with Killay Community Council Public Rights of Way Committee, helping to walk footpaths and bridlepaths in the Killay part of the ward and report issues to the Countryside Access Team.
Attended an Alzheimer's Society event at the invitation of a local resident.
Took part in the memorial service organised by Ebeneser Chapel to mark the centenary of the Killan Mining Disaster. Honoured to be asked to give a reading.
Worked with the Council's Gower National Landscape team to secure refurbishment of the Killan Mining Disaster memorial.
Supported the campaign to save the Ospreys, signing and sharing the petition, attending the public meeting called by Cllr Rob Stewart and passing on correspondence from residents.
Supported Dunvant RFC, personally sponsoring an advertising hoarding at the ground and using my community budget to help fund new floodlights.
Made a donation to Killay Lunch Club to help fund the ongoing hire of St Hilary's.
Funded the printing of songbooks and orders of service for the Forget Me Not dementia club carol concert at Siloam Chapel.
Worked with Killay Community Council and Dunvant RFC on a large community event for the Queen's Platinum Jubilee.
Invited to attend the local community Holi event at Killay Scout and Guide HQ.

Rewarding local volunteers for their efforts with access to free Swansea City FC tickets, including Nicci, who makes one of the brilliant postbox toppers, and Michelle, who volunteers at Social Centre events.
Trained as a Health Walk Leader so I can work with Friends of Dunvant Park and other community groups to organise short wellbeing walks in the area.

Joined Bikeability Wales on its leg of the Cerebra Relay Your Way event, raising money and awareness of the work to champion the 1.5 million disabled young people in the UK and promote inclusive sport, adventure and play.
Funded hats, T-shirts and signage for Bikeability based at Dunvant RFC.

Organising annual CPR and defibrillator training sessions with Heartbeat Trust UK at various Dunvant and Killay venues, including St Hilary's, Dunvant RFC and Gospel Hall, Dunvant Road.

Keeping residents informed about delays to refuse and recycling collections, chasing up missed collections and arranging replacement bags and bins.

councillors.name: Louise Gibbard
bio: It's been a real honour and privilege to serve as a councillor for Dunvant since 2017, and for the whole of Dunvant and Killay since 2022.

Hopefully, lots of you will know me already; I’m a governor at both Pen Y Fro and Dunvant Primary Schools, Secretary of the Friends of Dunvant Park, have organised lots of community events and I’m a regular litter picker across the area. Away from the ward, I’m the Chair of STOPP (Swansea Takes On Period Poverty), an active member of Unite Community Swansea branch and Joint Cabinet Member for Supporting Communities involved in making Council decisions around things like equalities and human rights, tackling domestic abuse and our community facilities across Swansea.
I’m passionate about public service, and doing my bit to represent local people and working with you to make improvements to our lovely area.

paras.label: Then
paras.text: Monks from Neath Abbey worked this land from the 12th century, and Melin Mynach, “the monks' mill”, still carries their name. Wool from Cwrt y Carnau is said to have reached Flanders and Italy. Gorseinon grew quickly in the late 1800s and early 1900s around steel, tinplate and coal, and the railway carried its tinplate and coal to Swansea Docks. Grovesend had its own works from 1900 and collieries at Grovesend, Brynlliw and Tir Isaf. St Teilo's Church, which stood on the marsh at Castell Ddu for centuries, was taken down stone by stone and rebuilt at St Fagans National Museum of History.

paras.label: Today
paras.text: Around 11,100 people live in Gorseinon, Penyrheol, Grovesend and Waungron. New homes such as Bryngwyn Village stand on the old works sites, while farms including Llannant, Cwrt y Carnau, Gwynfaen and Pencefnarda run down to the River Loughor. The town centre, Parc y Werin, Parc Melin Mynach and Golden Grove Park are at the heart of community life, and more people here speak Welsh than the Swansea average.

bio: I was elected as Labour councillor for Gowerton in May 2022. I live 500 metres from the stream that separates Waunarlwydd from Gowerton, and I’m the fourth generation of my family to live in Waunarlwydd. I have always loved being involved in my local community: I’m a member of Waunarlwydd RFC and one of the organisers of the Waunarlwydd Carnival, which raised around £5,000 a year for charity before Covid.

On the council I chair the scrutiny working group on taxi services, and I sit on the Petitions Committee and on scrutiny panels and working groups covering highways maintenance, street scene, public toilets, grants, and regeneration and finance.

councillors.name: Cyril Anderson
bio: Cyril, elected May 2015, is Swansea born & bred with strong roots in the ward. He is a school governor on both Seaview & Townhill primary schools, and he works closely with community & charity groups, and is very vocal when it comes to speaking out on behalf of local Issues.

He is very keen on providing opportunities for children, such as the new play areas that have been constructed at Mayhill Park. But he is equally keen to help support the elderly and the vulnerable, and has always been actively involved in TOPIC House, the Older People's Information Centre.
He chairs the Economy, Environment & Infrastructure Policy Development Committee which helps to achieve the aims of the council.
Cyril has been an activist in the Labour Party for well over 15 years, and a union man for many years, and is married.

councillors.name: David Hopkins
bio: David, who is also Swansea born & bred, has been a councillor representing this ward for over 30 years and is well known across the ward. He served as the Lord Mayor of Swansea for 16-17, and now shares the demanding roles of both Deputy Leader, as well as being the Cabinet Member for Delivery.

He is also currently governor at Townhill primary school. He has always dealt with ward issues as a priority and works hard behind the scenes to get things done, such as securing additional funding to replace the All Weather Pitch at the Phoenix Centre, and ensure funding for the construction of the new play areas on Mayhill Park.
He has been a member of the Labour Party for over 40 years, and a member of Unite union. David is married with 3 three grown up children and three grandchildren.

councillors.name: Lesley Walton
bio: Lesley got elected in 2012 and has been a school governor ever since, at Seaview Primary and currently at Dylan Thomas Community School. Knowing the issues which face the ward she is keen to promote the local Swansea Bay Credit Union, where members can borrow at a reasonable interest, & save money.
She has also been particularly involved in the setting up of the Friends of Mayhill Washing Lake & Community Food Garden, to address flytipping issues and provide communal food.
As Diversity Champion she speaks up at committee meetings, on social media, and uses her house front window to promote events. She is looking forward to helping Swansea become a Human Rights City.
She has been a Labour Party & union member, currently Unite, for over 35 years. Lesley is married with two cats, and runs her own design & print business.

councillors.name: Rebecca Fogarty
bio: An active member of the community since moving here in 2016, I am Vice Chair of Mumbles Community Council and a Governor at Mayals Primary School. I am active in a local church and volunteer on local environmental projects.

I have varied work experience in the public and charity sectors. I now work in public health so it’s been a busy couple of years for me! I led the local community council response to the first wave of the Covid-19 pandemic, ensuring all residents had access to essential food and prescriptions.

As a new Mam, you’ll often see me out with the pram. I want all generations in West Cross to enjoy good physical and mental well-being. I believe in involving people and bringing the community together to improve our local area. I’ve enjoyed talking to residents about varied issues, and look forward to meeting you in the near future.

councillors.name: Sara Keeton
bio: I’m a Mumbles Community Councillor and Chair of the Environmental Committee; also, I chair West Cross Community Centre Management Committee. I'm a School Governor at The Grange and YGG Llwynderw.

Living in West Cross nearly all my life, I've spent many years raising my family here. I have volunteered at local schools and with mental health and learning disability organisations over the years. I ran a business with my husband and my current work places me in the heart of the community.

I love West Cross and want it to remain a safe and fun place to be, to grow up and to grow older! Our fabulous community benefits from Mumbles and Gower being so close and still has strong links with the rest of Swansea. I want more opportunities for our residents to enjoy being part of what's on offer and to create more local interest groups, clubs and socials.
